A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QNPG research work. The main text, algorithms, equations, and complete Appendices A-F are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithmic constructions and theoretical convergence and query-complexity guarantees. Neither the main text nor Appendices A-F report original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical study and proof appendices. Its added explanatory and future-work passages introduce no original empirical results.

M1.justification: The trajectory estimators, quantum variance reduction, inner SGD loop, and classical policy updates remain unchanged in Algorithms 1-3 and equations (14)-(21). Added block-ending keywords clarify existing pseudocode structure without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on datasets or concrete MDP benchmarks. Actor-critic and constrained RL appear in v2 only as future directions, not newly evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Both retain theoretical literature comparisons with classical NPG and quantum stochastic optimization. Neither evaluates baseline methods experimentally; v2's additional citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports an empirical evaluation protocol. The theoretical prescriptions for H, N, K, learning rates, and target estimator variances are unchanged.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or case studies are added or removed. The appendices retain the same oracle constructions, estimator analysis, and convergence proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, error bars, or statistical tests. The theoretical mean-estimation success probabilities and variance guarantees also remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Neither contains empirical result entries. The theoretical outcomes are unchanged, including Theorem 3's epsilon^-1.5 query-complexity scaling up to logarithmic factors and O(epsilon^-1) iteration complexity.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, and proofs in Appendices A-F are retained. Section 4.2 adds a prose overview of the Lemma 6 proof, without changing its derivation or bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty and contribution claims: quantum-compatible NPG estimation, exponentially decaying truncation bias, and improved query complexity over classical NPG. These claims are neither strengthened nor narrowed.

C2.justification: v2's conclusion newly identifies quantum actor-critic algorithms and quantum extensions of constrained RL as open directions, adding specific discussion of unaddressed settings. Existing interpretations of truncation bias and the inner-loop quantum speedup remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The oracle/register constructions in Appendix A, variance-reduction subroutines in Appendix B, and parameter prescriptions in Section 4.3 and Appendix F are retained. No implementation, hardware, runtime, or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dong et al. (2008) to the QRL background and Gaur et al. (2024), Ganesh et al. (2025), and Mondal and Aggarwal (2024b) for the new future directions. Ganguly et al.'s publication update refers to the same existing work; the central novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are preserved. v2 adds a short Lemma 6 proof overview, future-work paragraph, acknowledgment, and generic impact statement, alongside limited copyedits and conference front matter. Its new running header incorrectly uses 'MPG' instead of 'NPG'.

P2.justification: v1 uses a single-column layout throughout; v2 substantially reformats the main text and references into two columns, adds conference title styling and running headers, and reflows equations and algorithm displays. The appendices remain single-column. Neither version contains scientific figures or data tables.

improvement.justification: The new Lemma 6 overview explains how contraction and bias/variance residuals fit together, modestly improving accessibility. The conclusion also connects specific unaddressed extensions to relevant literature. The method, guarantees, and proofs remain unchanged. Extensive reformatting is mainly presentational, and the new 'MPG' header typo is a small drawback; the net gain is limited to exposition and context.
